title: Normalized common finite-field models for supported lisse scalar extensions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put
$$C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega):f(P)\subset E'\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E'\subset\Omega\},\qquad B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$$
[sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $c:C\to B$ be inclusion. For a scheme $V$ over $X$ set $C_V=p_V^*C$, $B_V=p_V^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and for a finite intermediate field $D\subset\Omega$ put $A_{D,V}=p_V^*C(-,D)$, with its restricted norm topology [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Work on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with K-flat derived scalar extension and unit $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars].

Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ be constructible locally closed immersions [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], and define $h_!=i_*j_!$ for each such immersion $h=i\circ j$, with $j$ open into its closure and $i$ closed, using the exact module functors [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Fix finite intermediate fields $E,F\subset\Omega$ and lisse $A_{E,S}$- and $A_{F,T}$-modules $L,M$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $E_0=EF$ denote the smallest subfield of $\Omega$ containing $E,F$, and set $A_V=A_{E_0,V}$.

Then $X$ and the closures used in these factorizations are Noetherian, and their open subsets are quasi-compact. The field $E_0$ is finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The ordinary scalar extensions $L_0=A_S\otimes_{A_{E,S}}L$ and $M_0=A_T\otimes_{A_{F,T}}M$ represent the corresponding derived extensions of $L[0],M[0]$ and are lisse. Put $K=(a_!L_0)[0]$ and $N=(b_!M_0)[0]$. The objects $K,N$ are bounded constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

For $R=C,B$ write $S_R(V)=R_X\otimes^L_{A_X}V$, and define
$$G=a_!(C_S\otimes^L_{A_{E,S}}L[0]),\qquad H=b_!(C_T\otimes^L_{A_{F,T}}M[0]),\qquad J=B_X\otimes^L_{C_X}(-).$$
There are natural isomorphisms $\alpha:G\simeq S_CK$, $\beta:H\simeq S_CN$, $\alpha_B:JG\simeq S_BK$, $\beta_B:JH\simeq S_BN$. They are the K-flat scalar reassociations and the normalized support comparisons, linear over the destination ring. For an open support factor the comparison restricts to the identity under the open unit. For a closed support factor its open restriction is zero and its closed restriction is scalar pullback comparison followed by the original closed counit, under the new closed counit. These specifications apply on the full unbounded categories.

With $U=\operatorname{Res}_c$, $\eta:1\to UJ$ its scalar unit, and $m_V:\operatorname{Res}_{A_X\to C_X}S_CV\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_X\to B_X}S_BV$ the map induced by $c_X$, the identifications satisfy
$$U(\alpha_B)\circ\eta_G\circ\alpha^{-1}=m_K,\qquad U(\beta_B)\circ\eta_H\circ\beta^{-1}=m_N$$
after restriction to $A_X$. Successive units are identified with the direct unit by $(v\otimes z)\otimes w\mapsto v\otimes c_X(z)w$. These comparisons hold equally in the section-ring module model, under the equivalence preserving underlying abelian sheaves, derived tensors, internal Homs, support extension and the specified scalar adjunctions. Both supports and finite fields are independent; empty supports and rank zero are allowed. No flatness of $c_X$ or boundedness of the scalar extensions is assumed.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-heart-locally-closed-extension] to both immersions: their scheme-theoretic closures, the supports, and all open/closed subschemes used below are Noetherian, every open immersion in them is quasi-compact, and $h_!=i_*j_!$ is exact on modules and termwise on unbounded derived categories. In particular a sheaf extended in degree zero stays in degree zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite-type setting and exact support models

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] with base $\mathbf Q_\ell$, $K=E$ and $M=F$. It makes $EF/F$ finite. If $(e_i)$ spans $EF$ over $F$ and $(f_j)$ spans $F$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, the finitely many products $f_je_i$ span $EF$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$: expand each coefficient of $\sum_i a_ie_i$ in the $f_j$. Thus $E_0=EF$ is finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Its inclusions from $E,F$ and into $\Omega$ have the restricted norm topology, hence are continuous and induce the displayed coefficient maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), choose a common finite coefficient field

proof.text: For $L$ apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $A_{E,S}\to A_S$, and for $M$ apply it on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $A_{F,T}\to A_T$. The lisse hypothesis is precisely its local finite-free hypothesis [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. It gives canonical natural identifications of the derived extensions with $L_0[0],M_0[0]$, and says $L_0,M_0$ are locally finite free with the same ranks. In particular both are lisse, including rank zero. These internal-module assertions follow from their sectionwise versions through the exact tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] and the scalar-adjunction comparison [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction].

source.place: (1), K-flat realization of locally free scalar extensions

proof.text: Fix $h:S\hookrightarrow X$, $P=L_0$ (and repeat for $b,M_0$). Write $h=i\circ j$ through $Z=\overline S$. The ringed open/closed identities [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], transported by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], give $(i_*j_!P)|_S\cong P$, zero restriction on $Z\setminus S$ by $i_{Z\setminus S}^*j_!=0$, and zero restriction on $X\setminus Z$ by $j_{X\setminus Z}^*i_*=0$. The three nonempty members among $S,Z\setminus S,X\setminus Z$ form a finite constructible locally closed stratification: $S$ is open in the closed $Z$, and $Z\setminus S$ is closed in $X$. On $S$ the local model is $A_S\otimes_{E_0}E_0^{r}$, and on the other strata it is $A\otimes_{E_0}0$. The modules $E_0^{r}$ and zero are finitely presented. This verifies exactly [sk-def-sfb-constructible], so $K,N$ are bounded constructible, with cohomology only in degree zero.

For every coefficient map used here, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] supplies the exact abelian adjunctions, mixed zero restrictions and actual localization short exact sequence. The restrictions $j^{-1},i^{-1}$ are the exact inverse images $a^*$ of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] for the immersions $a=j,i$. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-open-closed-unbounded-calculus] to obtain these same adjunction maps and their triangle identities on the full unbounded derived categories. The scalar inverse-image comparison is the invertible mate $\theta$ of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. For an open factor take the comparison $T_Xj_!\cong j_!T_S$ of [lem-sfb-open-scalar-conjugate-normalization]; its displayed equation says its restriction is the identity under the open units and inverse-image tensor comparison. For a closed factor take $\delta:T_Xi_*\cong i_*T_Z$ of [lem-sfb-closed-supported-scalar-comparison]; it has zero open restriction and its closed restriction is $T_Z(\varepsilon_A)\theta_i^{-1}$ under $\varepsilon_B$. Thus each factor has exactly the required destination-linear normalization, without imposing flatness or a cohomological bound.

source.place: (1)-(2), normalized open and closed scalar comparisons

proof.text: Denote by $d_h^{D,R}:S_Rh_{!,D}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{!,R}S_R$ the composite through the fixed closed and open factors of step 5. The exact extension and restriction comparisons are those of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. Their hypotheses hold by step 1 and the cartesian pulled-back coefficients. The conditional coherence lemma [lem-sfb-normalized-immersion-comparison-coherence] therefore identifies these composites with the normalized locally closed comparisons. To verify its scalar-tower premise, use the balanced inverse-image square [lem-sfb-scalar-inverse-image-tower-diagram] on flat-term K-flat representatives; these stay flat-term K-flat under inverse image and under each scalar extension by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] (identity coefficient map, resp. identity topos), so every comparison in the square is evaluated on such representatives. The square's two arrows both send $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $t\,b(s)\otimes h^{-1}x$. Localizing gives the required square, with associator [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]; the K-flat comparison is precisely the specified one by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Thus the support comparisons commute with scalar reassociation, for all the coefficient towers $E\to E_0\to C\to B$ and $F\to E_0\to C\to B$.

source.place: (2)-(3), assembly and tower compatibility of support comparisons

proof.text: Write $q_E:S_{E\to E_0}L[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}L_0[0]$ for step 3. Reassociation gives $r_E:C_S\otimes^L_{A_{E,S}}L[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}C_S\otimes^L_{A_S}L_0[0]$ by first inserting the inverse associator and then $S_Cq_E$ [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Define $\alpha=(d_a^{E_0,C})^{-1}\circ a_!(r_E):G\xrightarrow{\sim}S_CK$. Repeat with $F,M,b$ to define $\beta$. Let $t_V:JS_CV\xrightarrow{\sim}S_BV$ be the same normalized associator for $A_X\to C_X\to B_X$, and set $\alpha_B=t_K\circ J\alpha$, $\beta_B=t_N\circ J\beta$. These are natural destination-linear isomorphisms. By the tower identity in step 6 these formulas equal the direct $B$-support comparisons after reassociation from $E$ or $F$; hence their open and closed restrictions have the normalizations in step 5.

source.place: (3), construct the four comparison isomorphisms from the normalized factors

proof.text: Naturality of the actual scalar unit for the $C_X$-linear map $\alpha$ gives $U(J\alpha)\eta_G=\eta_{S_CK}\alpha$. Consequently $U(\alpha_B)\eta_G\alpha^{-1}=U(t_K)\eta_{S_CK}$. The latter equals $m_K$: choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ of $K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; scalar extension preserves this class [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. On $C_X\otimes_{A_X}P$, the unit followed by reassociation sends $z\otimes v$ first to $1\otimes(z\otimes v)$ and then to $c_X(z)\otimes v$, which is exactly the map induced by $c_X$. These are maps of the same representative complexes, so their localizations agree. The units and associator have precisely these representative formulas [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization, lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. The calculation for $\beta$ is identical with $N$ in place of $K$. With module-first tensor notation, the same associator is $(v\otimes z)\otimes w\mapsto v\otimes c_X(z)w$, so inserting $z=w=1$ identifies successive units with the direct unit, as asserted.

Finally [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] preserves underlying sheaves, tensors, flatness and K-flat representatives; [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] identifies the scalar adjunctions and their actual units. The support functors and their units/counits are preserved by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], and the derived internal Homs, including evaluation, by [lem-sfb-module-object-ringed-site-derived-comparison]. Thus all the displayed constructions and equations carry to the section-ring model. Each argument was made separately for $(a,E,L)$ and $(b,F,M)$ using only their common compositum; neither supports nor original fields were identified. Empty strata may be omitted and rank-zero local models are zero, so the same construction covers empty supports and zero modules. The unbounded calculus and K-flat comparisons used above impose no flatness of $c_X$ and no bound on $S_CK$ or $S_BK$.
